name: Joe Kent
role: Former Director, National Counterterrorism Center (July 2025 to March 2026); former Republican congressional candidate, Washington's 3rd District (2022, 2024)
summary: Joe Kent is a former Army Green Beret and CIA officer who became a Republican politician. He campaigned on 'America First' themes, immigration restriction, and opposition to gun restrictions and federal health care. In 2026 he resigned as NCTC director, saying he opposed the Iran war and criticising Israeli influence; he has also made claims about the 2020 election and January 6 defendants that were widely disputed.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said 'the last thing the federal government should do is get involved in healthcare' (2022) and called for repealing the Affordable Care Act.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposes taxing couples earning $400,000 or more, saying it 'will directly impact' those earning less, and pledges not to raise federal income taxes.

unions-good.rationale: Opposes the PRO Act, saying it 'forces workers to join unions', and called teachers' union leaders 'thugs'.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Called to 'aggressively deregulate our natural resource industries' and criticised 'excessive regulation coming from the EPA' (2022). This concerns resource industries, not corporations generally.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Says marijuana conviction policy is 'a states' issue' and supports Washington state legalization but not federal legalization. Mixed.

limit-guns.rationale: Said he opposes 'any effort to further restrict firearm ownership' (2022) and 'I disagree with my opponent's call for new gun control limiting citizens' access to firearms' (OPB questionnaire, 2022).

empower-police-military.rationale: Backs funding 'constitutional sheriffs' and opposes Washington's law requiring police to use the least force necessary, but also says 'defund the FBI' (2024). Mixed.

decide-locally.rationale: Said 'Get the federal government out of our schools' (2022) and favoured local control of natural resources. Stated for schools and resources, not for every decision.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says 'I am pro-life', with an exception when a mother's life is at risk (2022). In 2024 he said he does not support a national abortion ban and that states should decide.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Called for mass deportations, building a wall, ending DACA and 'zero pathway to citizenship for illegals or their children' (2024 campaign statements).

free-trade.rationale: Advocated tariffs and 'economic sticks and carrots' to bring jobs back to the US (2022), and said 'slave labor in China' pushes down wages.

nation-first.rationale: No recorded position. Saying the government should not be directed by a foreign government is a related point; he did not weigh national interest against global cooperation.

open-borders.rationale: Said the four-plus years of 'open borders in this country' were 'incredibly dangerous' and that 'we have no idea who is in our country' (2026).

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called the green agenda 'a stalking horse to make America weak', said renewable energy is 'a payday for the Chinese Communist Party', and said 'we're in a warming cycle' without saying carbon emissions are definitively the cause (2022).

expand-nuclear.rationale: Supports long-term investment in nuclear power (OPB questionnaire, 2022).

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Advocated using tariffs and 'economic sticks and carrots to bring good paying jobs and rising wages back to the US' (2022).

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Supports reducing federal spending to control inflation and criticised 'printing money to finance Biden and Pelosi's agenda' (OPB questionnaire, 2022).

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Said increasing 'domestic production' is the cleanest path and called to 'reopen domestic energy production' (OPB questionnaire, 2022).

elite-replacement.rationale: Said 'the administration is trying to replace' American citizens through immigration (guides.vote summary of his statements, 2024). Low because it is a secondhand summary and names the administration rather than elites.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Describes a 'ruling class' managing 'the managed decline of our nation' (2024 campaign statements). Says Trump's circle was 'very, very tight' (2026). Low because 'corrupt' is not stated.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Reported as calling Putin's demands for Donetsk and Luhansk, and terms including Ukrainian neutrality, 'very reasonable' (2022, secondhand via Wikipedia).

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Agreed with a host's proposal to 'privatize' Social Security for younger workers through individual savings accounts (Lars Larson Show, 2022), while saying retirees and those near retirement would not change. Limited to younger workers, hence medium.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: No recorded position. His remarks on 'the trans agenda' and Pride flags do not address legal recognition of gender identity.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Called the Iran war 'completely avoidable' and said Iran posed 'no imminent threat' (2026); said 'wars are good for generals' (2021). Covers his opposition to starting wars, with targeted counterterrorism operations still in his view.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Opposes further firearm restrictions and said 'the American people should have the exact same weapons that our military has'. This reads against disarming citizens.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Called President Biden's loan forgiveness plan 'a complete disgrace & abuse of power' and opposes student loan forgiveness.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Opposes the PRO Act because it 'forces workers to join unions', which is the compulsory membership this statement rejects.

voter-id.rationale: Said 'I wish we could go back to voting in person where you actually had to show your ID' (2024), and called for reforms so that 'only people eligible to vote are doing so' (2022).

close-ties-china.rationale: Criticised China for 'raking in the cash' and called its gains from 'slave labor' and Communist Party 'payday' from renewables (2022 and 2026 remarks). Hostile to China rather than to close ties in general.

notes: Known answers are limited to sourced statements. Most campaign quotations come from an undated third-party compilation (guides.vote) and are marked low or medium where undated. The joekent.com and joekentforcongress.com campaign sites and the Washington State Standard and KGW debate coverage could not be opened (not found or HTTP 403). The Senate hearing transcript and the full resignation letter were not reachable. Kent's 2026 Shawn Ryan transcript is an unofficial repost; the full text was not read past the first 100,000 characters. Contested points: his claims about Israel, the Jan. 6 'political prisoners' framing, and the 2024 abortion position.
